How to get the most out of your smartphone/tablet/laptop Li-Ion rechargeable batteries | ZDNet
I was disappointed the article didn't mention portable chargers. I'd like to know if I'm frying my battery.

I agree with most of these points, but I have a bit of an issue with the bit about chargers. The writer describes them like they are actively shoving power into your phone, and that will damage the battery. The reality is that the phone will use as much power as it wants, and the only limit is the maximum current rating on the charger. Older chargers are usually rated for only 500-700 milliamps, which is why smartphones default to slow charging. They only fast charge when they detect the quick-charging circuitry (either built into the USB cable or the charger itself,) which lets the phone know it can draw more current (usually 1-2 amps) without blowing up the charger. I can only really see a charger damaging a phone if the voltage is not a steady 5V, which is entirely possible if you're using 5-cent wall warts off ebay.
